slides.title: In Italy, a latte is just milk
slides.subtitle: Order one at a bar and you may get a glass of milk.

slides.title: Latte means milk
slides.body: In Italian, latte is simply the word for milk. The drink you know from home comes from caffellatte, short for caffè e latte: coffee and milk.
slides.highlight: Latte = milk. Caffellatte = coffee and milk.

slides.title: So what should you order?
slides.body: Ask for a caffellatte: coffee with hot milk, in Italy usually a breakfast drink made at home. Or ask for a latte macchiato: steamed milk marked with espresso.

slides.label: At the bar
slides.body: Add one word. Say caffellatte or latte macchiato. Say only latte and the barista may hand you a glass of milk, no joke intended.

slides.title: Latte is milk. Coffee needs its word.
slides.body: Caffellatte for coffee and milk, latte macchiato for milk marked with espresso.
